name: Tunisia
sources: GDP $12.3bn: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series TUN, 1990 = 12,290,568,182 current US$, retrieved from the World Bank API 2026-08-12. The smallest economy in this region and the richest per head of the non-oil ones: $1,476 a person against Morocco's $1,229 (World Bank NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, 1990).

Population 8.3m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, TUN 1990 = 8,324,509. Tunisia had the lowest fertility in the Arab world, the legacy of the Code of Personal Status of 13 August 1956, and it is why this is the one North African state whose population is not doubling underneath its economy.

Interest rate 11.5%: UNVERIFIED. I could not retrieve a 1990 observation of the Central Bank of Tunisia's money-market rate (TMM) - the BCT's published series does not reach back that far in any form I could open. 11.5% is entered as the money-market rate under the liberalisation that began with the structural adjustment programme of 1986 and continued through Tunisia's GATT accession in 1990, and it implies a real rate of plus 5.0%: the tightest stance in this region, which is the correct sign for a country deliberately holding the dinar while it opened its capital account. The magnitude is a judgement and should be checked.

Revenue 28% of GDP: World Bank GC.TAX.TOTL.GD.ZS gives tax revenue at 19.95% of GDP for TUN 1990; 28% adds non-tax receipts and social contributions. The addition is an estimate and is DECLARED UNVERIFIED; the 19.95% underneath it is transcribed. Set above Morocco's 24% because Tunisia's state was proportionally larger and its social insurance older.

Investment 24% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, TUN 1990 = 24.36% gross fixed capital formation. The 9/15 split between public and private is NOT a published series and is DECLARED UNVERIFIED. It sits between Algeria's state-dominated 19/8 and Morocco's private-led 6/20, which is where Tunisia's own reform sat: the eighth plan opened tourism and textiles to private capital while the state kept the phosphate industry and the utilities.
Debt 65% of GDP: World Bank DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, TUN 1990 = 64.7%, total external debt stocks over GNI - EXTERNAL debt, on the same disclosed basis as the other files in this region.

Oil 0.09 mbd: transcribed from the Energy Institute / BP Statistical Review primary oil production series as republished by Our World in Data (Tunisia 1990 = 55.1 TWh) and converted against the roster entries already on that series (UK 1,065 TWh at 1.9 mbd, Egypt 529 TWh at 0.87 mbd). The conversion is mine, so the figure is DECLARED UNVERIFIED. El Borma and Ashtart, past peak since 1980, and enough to matter to a $12bn economy without making it a petro-state.
Military 1.8% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), TUN 1990 = 1.84%.

Strength 2: an abstract index, and the lowest entered in the roster so far. About 35,000 personnel with no armour worth the name. The deliberate policy of Bourguiba and then Ben Ali was an army too small to take the state - which is why the man who took the state in November 1987 was the interior minister and not a general. Set at a quarter of Egypt's 14 and an eighth of Italy's 26.

Stability 60: Ben Ali two years into a constitutional coup that had removed a senile president without a shot, a National Pact signed by every legal party on 7 November 1988, and an economy growing. Against that: the April 1989 election had just demonstrated that the system could not admit an opposition, and the confrontation with Ennahda that would fill the next three years had already started. Set at Egypt's 58 and below Morocco's 62.

Separatism 0.02: the lowest in the roster. Tunisia is the one state in this region with no minority nationality of any size, no contested province and no irredenta - a fact of Ottoman and French administrative history, and one of the reasons the model should not expect the Maghreb's troubles to look alike. Set below France's 0.03.

Authoritarianism 0.70: a hegemonic-party state, modelled the way this table models Egypt's. The Chamber of Deputies election of 2 April 1989 was contested and its result was arithmetically impossible: the Constitutional Democratic Rally took 80.57% of the vote and all 141 seats, and independents backed by Ennahda took 13.68% and none. A system in which a seventh of the electorate returns nobody is not one a vote can remove. Set below Egypt's 0.75 because the 1989 election was at least a real contest, and above Morocco's 0.65 because Morocco's opposition at least sat in the chamber.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.4569%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series TUN (Tunisia): 7,220,044 in 1984 to 8,151,660 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: TUN.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 93% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 636 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: TUN, 1989 = 636 subscriptions and 1990 = 953 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: TUN, 1990 = 93%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
